title: Runtime 1.22 RC Release Notes — KV Cache Compaction + Tier-Aware Eviction
content:
> **Archived 2026-02-12:** this page is superseded by "Runtime 1.22 Release Notes — KV Cache Compaction + Tier-Aware Eviction" and is kept for reference only.

## Summary
The Runtime 1.22 release candidate adds **KV cache compaction** and **tier-aware KV eviction**. Together they target GPU memory fragmentation and the burst-driven p95/p99 tail latency we see on sustained decode workloads with mixed sequence lengths.

Included in the RC:
- A **fragmentation-aware allocator health model** with new fragmentation metrics and allocator state tracking.
- **Budgeted compaction** (time and bytes) wired into the scheduler so decode is not stalled.
- A **tier-aware eviction policy** (LRU-by-sequence plus safety constraints) to avoid chaotic evictions during bursts.
- **Tracing spans and exemplars** linking compaction/eviction events to tail latency.
- A **kill-switch** and rollout knobs so oncall can turn compaction/eviction off quickly.

Expected impact:
- Less tail latency variance under bursts and churn.
- Fewer allocator-thrash episodes and fragmentation-driven OOM/forced shedding.
- Negligible steady-state throughput cost when budgets hold.

---

## Who is impacted
**Internal:** Runtime, SRE, Release Engineering, Support, Solutions/CS, Product (Hosted + Dedicated).

**External:** Hosted and Dedicated customers, and Private clusters where the owner enables it. No API changes; only runtime memory management under load changes.

---

## What changed (high-level)
### 1) Compaction (new)
When fragmentation crosses the trigger threshold, the runtime **relocates KV pages** to make the KV arena more contiguous. Work is incremental and budgeted.
- Budget applies per scheduler phase.
- Compaction yields whenever latency-sensitive work is waiting.
- Relocations are counted and traced; correctness has been tested under cancellation and churn.

### 2) Tier-aware eviction (new)
If allocator pressure stays high and compaction can't recover headroom fast enough, KV entries may be evicted by:
- **Tier priority** (lower tiers first)
- **Recency** (LRU-by-sequence)
- **Safety constraints** (pinned sessions and active decode are protected)

Eviction is a burst guardrail, not a steady-state mechanism.

### 3) Observability (expanded)
Standardized fragmentation/compaction/eviction metrics plus tracing spans for correlation.

---

## Default settings by tier (Runtime 1.22 RC)
Hosted defaults favor tail latency stability; Dedicated defaults are a bit more permissive.

> All settings are configurable per deployment profile. Private defaults to off unless explicitly enabled.

### Tier defaults table
| Tier | Compaction | Eviction | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hosted (Shared) | ON | ON (tier-aware) | Strict budgets; automated rollback criteria in the rollout system. |
| Dedicated | ON | OFF (opt-in) | Slightly higher compaction budgets; eviction enabled per pool on request. |
| Private (VPC / On-prem) | OFF (default) | OFF (default) | Enable per cluster after validating observability and headroom. |

### Runtime flags
Propagated through runtime config profiles:
- `kv.compaction.enabled` (bool)
- `kv.compaction.trigger_fragmentation_ratio` (float 0..1)
- `kv.compaction.budget_ms_per_step` (int)
- `kv.compaction.budget_bytes_per_step` (int)
- `kv.compaction.max_steps_per_tick` (int)
- `kv.eviction.enabled` (bool)
- `kv.eviction.policy` (string; default: `tier_aware_lru`)
- `kv.eviction.min_free_bytes_target` (int)
- `kv.eviction.protect_pinned_sessions` (bool; default: true)
- `kv.kill_switch` (bool; emergency disable compaction+eviction)

### Recommended defaults (RC)
Hosted (Shared):
- `kv.compaction.enabled = true`
- `kv.compaction.trigger_fragmentation_ratio = 0.25`
- `kv.compaction.budget_ms_per_step = 2`
- `kv.compaction.budget_bytes_per_step = 268435456` (256 MiB)
- `kv.compaction.max_steps_per_tick = 1`
- `kv.eviction.enabled = true`
- `kv.eviction.policy = tier_aware_lru`
- `kv.eviction.min_free_bytes_target = 2147483648` (2 GiB)
- `kv.kill_switch = false`

Dedicated:
- `kv.compaction.enabled = true`
- `kv.compaction.trigger_fragmentation_ratio = 0.35`
- `kv.compaction.budget_ms_per_step = 3`
- `kv.compaction.budget_bytes_per_step = 402653184` (384 MiB)
- `kv.compaction.max_steps_per_tick = 1`
- `kv.eviction.enabled = false` (opt-in per pool)
- `kv.kill_switch = false`

Private (VPC / On-prem):
- `kv.compaction.enabled = false` (default)
- `kv.eviction.enabled = false` (default)
- If enabling, start from Hosted budgets and confirm dashboards/alerts first.

Rationale: a low trigger ratio and tight budgets keep compaction from bunching into visible spikes; Dedicated pools have steadier load and can absorb more work per tick.

---

## Monitoring guidance
### Dashboards
Use the standard KV compaction panels overlaid with latency percentiles. During canary, watch at minimum:
- Fragmentation ratio (per model, per pool)
- Compaction bytes moved / sec
- Compaction step time (ms) and budget utilization
- Evictions / sec by tier and reason
- KV free bytes / headroom
- p50/p95/p99 latency on decode-heavy routes
- OOM / forced shedding signals

### Key metrics
- `runtime_kv_fragmentation_ratio`, `runtime_kv_free_bytes`, `runtime_kv_arena_bytes` (gauges)
- `runtime_kv_compaction_bytes_moved_total`, `runtime_kv_compaction_steps_total`, `runtime_kv_compaction_budget_exhausted_total` (counters)
- `runtime_kv_compaction_step_time_ms` (histogram)
- `runtime_kv_evictions_total{tier,reason}`, `runtime_kv_eviction_bytes_total{tier,reason}` (counters)
- Spans: `kv.compaction.step`, `kv.eviction.select`, `kv.eviction.execute`; exemplars carry model, pool, tier, relocation bytes and allocator watermark.

### What good looks like
- Fragmentation mostly below trigger; compaction intermittent.
- Step time close to budget (~1–3 ms) with low variance.
- Evictions rare, burst-only, back to ~zero afterwards.
- No p99 spikes lined up with compaction bytes moved.

### Rollout guardrails
- Hosted canaries auto-roll back when sustained p99 regression beyond the SLO guardrail correlates with compaction/eviction.
- Page on rising eviction rate together with rising fragmentation and falling free bytes.
- Dedicated: compare to pool baselines; no sustained throughput loss or rise in cancellation errors.

---

## Rollout plan
1. **Internal canary** (one region/pool, runtime-owned workloads)
2. **Hosted subset** (small share of Shared pools, latency-sensitive routes first)
3. **Dedicated pools** (opt-in per pool)
4. **Broader enablement** by region/model profile

Every phase needs metrics and dashboards in place and a tested kill-switch.

---

## Operational controls
### Kill-switch
1. Set `kv.kill_switch = true` on the affected pool/cluster.
2. Within ~1–2 config propagation intervals confirm `runtime_kv_compaction_steps_total` and `runtime_kv_evictions_total` stop increasing.
3. If still unstable, use standard overload/backpressure procedures.

### Common symptoms
- p99 spikes during bursts: inspect bytes moved/sec and step time; lower `kv.compaction.budget_ms_per_step` or raise the trigger ratio slightly; kill-switch if severe.
- Elevated evictions: check free bytes trend, fragmentation, tier breakdown; raise `kv.eviction.min_free_bytes_target` or adjust tier weights.
- OOM / forced shedding: check headroom and compaction progress; enable eviction if off, or adjust thresholds; consider capacity.

---

## Customer-facing notes (Support / CS)
- “Runtime 1.22 adds KV cache compaction and safer eviction to reduce fragmentation-related tail latency spikes in bursty workloads.”
- “No API changes; the improvements are in the serving runtime's memory manager.”
- Ask reporters for time window, region/pool, model and route, burst/concurrency evidence and request IDs for trace correlation.

---

## Known risks / limitations
- Oversized budgets can make compaction visible as latency spikes.
- Pinned-session protection can limit eviction effectiveness under extreme pressure.
- Heavy churn with frequent cancellations stresses relocation bookkeeping; monitor cancellation-related errors.

---
